subject: Renewal discussion: stability bridge, commit swap, and price-hold request
messages:
From: Anna James <anna.james@olivetech.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@olivetech.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning + request for price stability and commit swap

Hi Soojin,

Hope you had a good week. Our contract with Redwood comes up for renewal in June and leadership has asked procurement to push for two things before signing a renewal: a price-stability window for baseline usage and a more flexible committed volume that better matches our Q3/Q4 product launch profile.

We ran a usage slice for Q1 (attached) — we saw a big spike in inference traffic in March (new AB test). We like Redwood's throughput and the Dedicated proposition, but given the launch cadence we need both a predictable unit price for a period and the option to shift committed tokens between quarters without heavy penalty.

Can Redwood offer: 
- a short-term price hold on our baseline for 4-6 months,
- a mechanism to swap committed capacity between quarters (commit swap), and
- an option for bridge credits if we buy down-term commit but expect bursts?

If you can sketch options, we can mark which paths are acceptable to finance and exec. Attaching our Q1 usage and the current SOW for reference.

Thanks,
Anna
Anna James
Procurement Manager, OliveTech
anna.james@olivetech.com
+1 415-555-0198

Attachments: Olivetech_Usage_Q1_2027.csv (csv), Olivetech_SOW_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anna James <anna.james@olivetech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + request for price stability and commit swap

Hi Anna — thanks for the context and the usage export, that helps a lot. We have a few pragmatic paths we can propose so OliveTech keeps predictable margins while still supporting the launch spikes: 

Option A — Stability + True-up
- 6-month price hold on your baseline unit price (applies to committed baseline)
- Quarterly true-ups for burst overage at standard overage rate
- No changes to committed volume mid-term (fastest to implement)

Option B — Commit Swap + Bridge Credits (recommended for launch variability)
- Allow two commit swaps per year (move committed tokens between adjacent quarters)
- Provide bridge credits equal to 15% of the quarterly commit if you reduce a quarter's commit by more than 20% (applies once per rolling 12 months)
- 4-month price hold on baseline

Option C — Lower upfront commit + tiered discounting
- Reduce upfront commit by up to 25% and apply tiered discounting as volume scales; longer-term price hold negotiable with higher commit

I looped Ben to validate margin impact — attaching a sketch of the bridge pricing model. Can we hop on a 30-min call early next week to walk the options with Raj and finance? If the team prefers, we can also provide a redline of the SOW with Option B as a proposed language.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: Redwood_bridge_pricing_model.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: OLIVE - recommended concession framing

Soojin / Marcus — quick internal note ahead of the call with OliveTech: 

I recommend we frame the concession as a short-term margin trade to lock the customer into a multi-quarter relationship while protecting unit economics. Suggested commercial terms: 
- Effective discount: 9.5% off list on committed baseline (applies to first two quarters)
- Price hold: 6 months on committed baseline after renewal effective date
- Commit-swap: allow up to two swaps per 12 months; swaps trigger a small admin fee (0.5% of quarterly commit) unless the customer accepts a reduced bridge credit (we should avoid setting "free" swaps)
- Bridge credit: one-time credit equal to 12% of the reduced quarter's commit tokens (applied over the following two invoices)
- True-up cadence: quarterly, with overage charged at list overage rate

Margin impact: with these terms we protect ~85% of expected revenue while creating room for them to scale. Marcus — can you confirm whether the 12% bridge credit math fits within our promo budget?

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: internal_bridging_calcs.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@olivetech.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Anna James <anna.james@olivetech.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + request for price stability and commit swap

Thanks Soojin,

Helpful options. A couple of constraints from finance: we need the price hold to cover at least the first two quarters following renewal to stabilize our forecasts. We are uneasy about any administrative fees tied to swaps — that adds operational complexity for our treasury team. Our preference would be: 

- 6-month price hold on baseline (non-negotiable)
- Commit swaps allowed without admin fee if swaps are executed at least 30 days before the quarter start
- Bridge credits should be available but we prefer them to be applied as an invoice credit over the following one invoice, not spread out (simpler for accounting)

Also — if Redwood does the 6-month hold, can you tighten the bridge credit to 10% instead of 12%? That would be much easier for our CFO to sign off on.

If you can send a redlined SOW with those terms, we'll aim to route for approval next week.

Regards,
Raj Patel
Head of Finance, OliveTech
raj.patel@olivetech.com

Attachment: Olivetech_prelim_response.pdf (pdf)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@olivetech.com>, Anna James <anna.james@olivetech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 04 Apr 2027 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + request for price stability and commit swap

Raj / Anna — appreciate the clarity. We can accept the revised commercial points: 

- 6-month price hold on your committed baseline (effective at renewal)
- Commit swaps: up to two per 12 months, executed >=30 days before quarter start, no admin fee
- Bridge credit: 10% of the reduced quarter's commit applied as a single invoice credit on the following invoice
- Quarterly true-up for overage, standard overage rates apply
- We will include a commit-swap provision and the bridge-credit language in the redlined SOW and share a DocuSign package for signature.

I've attached the redline (Olivetech_SOW_v2-redline.pdf) and the DocuSign link for the SOW. If the commercial is acceptable, Anna — please confirm and we'll get legal to finalize. Ben / Marcus — once Anna confirms, please approve the DocuSign envelope for signature.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: Olivetech_SOW_v2-redline.pdf (pdf)
DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/olivetech/sow-v2
